entries.final_answer: Default topology by Mission size, reversing the #5100 explicit-only rule. single_branch when the finalized tasks have <=2 WPs or lane computation yields one lane; lanes otherwise. An explicit --topology always wins. Applied at finalize-tasks, because create runs before WPs exist. Needs an ADR. S8 must land before or with S7.

entries.final_answer: Restate it: lane checkouts never show the status files (sparse exclusion at every lane-checkout creation site, lanes topology included), lanes never change them (a write-check refuses), readers never read them (S1). A migration applies the exclusion to existing lane worktrees and reports, never drops, lane-only events. The fork-time blob stays in lane history.
entries.question: Escalation: physically deleting status files from lane branches would be carried onto the coordination/Mission branch by consolidation, trips auto-rebase and conflicts with ADR 2026-07-29-1 Assert A'. How is ruling 3 implemented?

entries.final_answer: Refuse plus attest: follow the lanes precedent. Every unstamped approval refuses APPROVAL_STAMP_MISSING, and the operator lifts it with --attest-approved-reviewed per WP.
entries.question: Escalation: in-flight single_branch Missions have unstamped approvals. What happens to existing Missions when the S8 approval bound is turned on?
entries.rationale: Operator ruling, stijn-dejongh, 2026-11-06 (epic #7276). Quoted as given.

entries.final_answer: Unless the mission is specified with an explicit topology being defined, no worktrees/lanes/coord branch should be created. A single topic branch for the mission is minted, regardless of default branch protected status. Once the topology is settled, and the finalization has completed -> lanes/worktrees are created. That solves the discrepancy rather naturally, and is more efficient (delay creation until the topology is chosen). Rationale: reworking and reminting topologies is expensive, and compressing a lanes/coord topology into a single_branch one is the most expensive approach. The inverse is a lot simpler to perform.

entries.final_answer: Seam now, amend later: extract one lane-cleanup module behind a remover port; kept lanes are reported, never a traceback after a verified landing; fix clear_tip gating and the resume crash window; draft the ADR 2026-11-06-1 amendment (local target at the gate-passed tip as landing proof; probe unavailable means keep and report). Bind the port to destructive_guard once #7275 merges.
